newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary royal back in public life after 50 years.
newsitem.headline: Hungary royal back in public life after 50 years.

text.p: Archduke Georg von Habsburg, grandson of the last king of Hungary, became the first Hungarian royal to serve his country in 50 years on Monday when he was sworn in as his country's Ambassador for European Integration.

"Having a Habsburg in the position (of ambassador) helps enhance the reputation and image of Hungary," Socialist Prime Minister Gyula Horn told reporters after the ceremony in the Parliament building.

Horn, a former communist, said the appointment was also a recognition of the work of von Habsburg's father Otto, now 84, an Austrian Euro MP and founder of the Pan-European movement who had pushed Hungary's case for European integration.
Von Habsburg, 32, is the grandson of Austria's last Emperor Karl, who was separately king of Hungary.
He has worked as a television journalist in several countries and will now be a roving ambassador affiliated to the prime minister's Office.
